thread_analysis.thread_summary: An internal Allion thread (entirely in English) coordinating Bluetooth RF PHY logo testing for an Alinco DUT at Allion's Taiwan HQ lab, between Allion Japan's PM Toshitaka Mochizuki, lab engineer Leo Chou, Ning Lin, and Itsuo Sakai, on behalf of an end customer (referenced as Alps Alpine in the thread, awaiting test completion). The thread runs from initial DUT shipment and test request (January 7, 2026) through DUT power-on and USB/driver/cable connection troubleshooting, an output-power-vs-declared-Power-Class-1 mismatch resolved via a test configuration correction rather than a hardware fix, and final report review confirming test completion (January 30, 2026).
all_questions_found: Why won't the DUT power on/stay connected properly, and why do LE HCI test commands fail even with the correct driver installed? (see thread_0231_case_01)
Does the DUT actually qualify as LE Power Class 1 given its below-10dBm measured output power, and should testing pause for a firmware/hardware fix? (see thread_0231_case_02)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread illustrates two categories of RF PHY test execution troubleshooting: physical/connection-layer issues (DUT power-on behavior, USB driver, and ultimately a USB cable swap) that blocked test commands from running at all, and a substantive test-configuration issue (an outdated SoC qualification under Core Specification v5.2 predating the LE Power Class 1 definition, making the IXIT's Power Class 1 declaration inapplicable) that was correctly diagnosed and resolved via a test-configuration change rather than a vendor firmware update.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Connection-layer test blockers should be diagnosed by isolating each potential failure point (power-on behavior misunderstanding, driver, cable) rather than assuming a single root cause; power-class declaration mismatches should be checked against the underlying SoC's original Core Specification qualification version before requesting a vendor hardware/firmware fix.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See thread_0231_case_01 and thread_0231_case_02 for specific risks.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The team's initial instinct (visible in Mochizuki's January 26 message) was to ask the customer to raise the DUT's output power via firmware before Sakai's January 28 correction identified the real issue as a test-configuration/Core-Spec-version mismatch — a brief misstep that was caught and corrected before it reached the customer as a firmware-update request, illustrating the value of escalating ambiguous test-classification issues to a senior reviewer (Sakai) before requesting customer-side hardware changes.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For RF PHY power-class mismatches, always check the underlying SoC's original Core Specification qualification version before concluding a hardware/firmware fix is needed — an older qualification version may not have defined the power class category being tested against at all, making a test-configuration correction the right fix instead of a costly vendor-side hardware change.
